message.content:
You own the TPU v6e PRE-SILICON lane for /workspace/SuperGrok1.5 (branch claude/h100-audit-maximal). No TPU exists yet; your mission is to make the TPU-side code CURRENT and FUNCTIONALLY CPU-VALIDATED so silicon day-1 is pure hardware bring-up. Three deliverables:

A. DRIFT CLOSURE. csrc/backends/pallas/ (18 files: launch_<opt>.py Pallas kernels + helpers) and csrc/fused/tpu_v6e/ (33 generated cell files) were last touched at commit 94a0b2e. The canonical optimizer math (csrc/algorithms/<opt>.h — THE single source, shared across sm_90/gfx942/tpu) and the sm_90 kernels evolved past them: run `git log --oneline 94a0b2e..HEAD` and `git diff 94a0b2e..HEAD -- csrc/algorithms/ grokking_optimizers/kernels/sm_90/` to build the work list. Port SEMANTIC/CORRECTNESS changes into the Pallas implementations: known hunt list — (1) Muon inverted weight-decay fix; (2) Prodigy: EMA d-adaptation semantics + the degree-2 d_prev^2 + |g| partials (canonical prodigy.h:48,52 — the Python ref in tests/hw/test_reference_parity.py::ref_prodigy_partials was JUST canonicalized, use it); (3) SG2: matrix-GRU + slow-EMA (slows) state + lamb_eff semantics; (4) SG11: cosine-gated mu semantics + lamb_eff = ramp*lamb*(1-gate)*alpha; (5) grokadamw: layer-wise beta1 vector semantics (per-tensor b1, bc1=1-b1^t) + the published alpha_t grokking-signal form (grokking_optimizers/optimizers/grokadamw.py documents it); (6) any bounds/indexing fixes. CUDA-idiom changes (PTX, vec4) do NOT port — Pallas has its own idioms; port only math/behavior. If a Pallas file re-inlines math that now disagrees with csrc/algorithms/<opt>.h, fix it to match canonical and cite the header lines.

B. INTERPRET-MODE PARITY (the big one). Install JAX CPU into the environment WITHOUT disturbing torch: first `python -c "import numpy; print(numpy.__version__)"`; then install jax pinned so numpy is NOT upgraded (e.g. `pip install jax ml_dtypes opt_einsum --no-deps` plus whatever pure-python deps are missing, checking each; NEVER let pip replace numpy/scipy/torch). After install verify BOTH `python -c "import torch; torch.zeros(2)+1"` AND `python -c "import jax; jax.numpy.zeros(2)"` work. (GPU is busy — CPU-only jax, do not install CUDA jax.) Then build tests/tpu/test_pallas_parity_interpret.py (NEW directory — create tests/tpu/__init__.py too): for EACH of the 11 optimizer Pallas kernels, run it under pl.pallas_call(..., interpret=True) on CPU against the fp64 reference functions in tests/hw/test_reference_parity.py (ref_adamw_step, ref_lion_step, ref_muon_step, ref_prodigy_*, ref_grokadamw_step, ref_grokfast_*, ref_sg11/sg15/sg2 apply refs, ref_neuralgrok, ref_looksam — read that file for the exact inventory) on randomized tensors (multiple sizes incl. odd/non-multiple-of-8, multiple seeds, nonzero initial state, several steps for stateful EMAs). Tolerances: these kernels are fp32 — use the fp32-vs-fp64 tolerance discipline that file already uses (read its ATOL/RTOL). Mark the suite so it's skipped when jax is absent (pytest.importorskip) and so CI stays green. Run the suite; fix Pallas-side bugs it finds (expect some — this is the first functional execution of these kernels ever; that is the point). If a kernel CANNOT run in interpret mode (TPU-only primitive), document exactly why and what silicon-day-1 must check.

C. CELL/COMPOSITION AUDIT. csrc/fused/tpu_v6e/*.py: inventory what the 33 cells actually compose (surrogate model? which optimizer entry points?), whether they reference Pallas functions that still exist post-drift-closure (import them in a dry-run if cheap), and what the real-model-stage program (the sm_90 oracle->mirror->kernel ladder for decoder/vit/mamba, see INTEGRATION-*.md) implies for their TPU twins — a written gap list, not an implementation.

HARD RULES: do not touch sm_90/gfx942 files, csrc/bindings/, dispatch.py, megakernel_codegen.py, tuning/, grokking_race_v2.py, tests/hw/ (READ yes, write no), model stage headers — sibling agents own them. New files only under tests/tpu/ + edits within csrc/backends/pallas/ and csrc/fused/tpu_v6e/. No functionality suppression: fix components, never stub them. Do not commit. GPU busy — everything CPU.

REPORT: per-file drift table (hunk -> classification -> ported/deferred); jax install footprint (exact packages added, numpy untouched proof); per-optimizer interpret-parity matrix (pass/fail/max-err per size/seed) + bugs found&fixed; the cell-audit gap list; the TPU silicon-day-1 checklist.

248	        _f64, (p, g, m, v, mu_state, slow_state))
249	    if torch.is_tensor(expert_out):
250	        expert_out = _f64(expert_out)
251	    mu_new = gru_decay * mu_state + (1.0 - gru_decay) * expert_out
252	    slow_new = alpha * slow_state + (1.0 - alpha) * g
253	    smart_grad = g + alpha * mu_new + lamb_eff * slow_new
254	    bc1 = 1.0 - beta1 ** t
255	    bc2 = 1.0 - beta2 ** t
256	    p_new, m_new, v_new = _adam_tail(p, m, v, smart_grad, lr, beta1, beta2,
257	                                     eps, wd, bc1, bc2)
258	    return p_new, m_new, v_new, mu_new, slow_new

261	# ── muon.h (+ bindings.cpp::muon_fused_step orchestration) ───────────────────
262	# NS coefficients are the canonical (3.4445, -4.7750, 2.0315) from
263	# csrc/bindings/bindings.cpp::muon_fused_step.
264	MUON_NS_A, MUON_NS_B, MUON_NS_C = 3.4445, -4.7750, 2.0315
265	
266	
267	def ref_muon_step(p, g, buf, *, momentum, lr, wd, ns_steps):
268	    """2D parameter update.
269	        buf = momentum*buf + grad                 (no (1-momentum); matches header)
270	        X   = buf / (||buf||_F + 1e-7)
271	        repeat ns_steps:  A=X@Xᵀ; AX=A@X; AAX=A@AX; X = a*X + b*AX + c*AAX
272	        scale = 0.2 * sqrt(max(rows, cols))
273	        p     = p*(1 - lr*wd) + (-lr*scale)*X
274	    Returns (p_new, buf_new).
275	    """
276	    p, g, buf = map(_f64, (p, g, buf))
277	    buf_new = momentum * buf + g
278	    inv_norm = 1.0 / (torch.linalg.norm(buf_new) + 1e-7)
279	    X = buf_new * inv_norm
280	    for _ in range(ns_steps):
281	        A = X @ X.t()
282	        AX = A @ X
283	        AAX = A @ AX
284	        X = MUON_NS_A * X + MUON_NS_B * AX + MUON_NS_C * AAX
285	    rows, cols = p.shape[0], p.shape[1]
286	    scale = 0.2 * math.sqrt(max(rows, cols))
287	    neg_lr_scale = -lr * scale
288	    decay = 1.0 - lr * wd
289	    p_new = p * decay + neg_lr_scale * X
290	    return p_new, buf_new

1	"""Pallas/TPU launch glue for AdamW.
2	
3	Algorithm: csrc/algorithms/adamw.h
4	Self-contained — inlines the per-tensor AdamW math (formerly imported
5	from primitives.py::adamw_step).
6	"""
7	
8	from __future__ import annotations
9	
10	import jax
11	import jax.numpy as jnp
12	from typing import Tuple
13	
14	
15	def launch_adamw_step(
16	    param: jnp.ndarray,
17	    exp_avg: jnp.ndarray,
18	    exp_avg_sq: jnp.ndarray,
19	    grad: jnp.ndarray,
20	    lr: float,
21	    beta1: float,
22	    beta2: float,
23	    eps: float,
24	    wd: float,
25	    bc1: float,
26	    bc2: float,
27	) -> Tuple[jnp.ndarray, jnp.ndarray, jnp.ndarray]:
28	    """Per-tensor AdamW step. Returns new (param, exp_avg, exp_avg_sq)."""
29	    m = beta1 * exp_avg + (1.0 - beta1) * grad
30	    v = beta2 * exp_avg_sq + (1.0 - beta2) * grad * grad
31	    m_hat = m / bc1
32	    v_hat = v / bc2
33	    update = m_hat / (jnp.sqrt(v_hat) + eps)
34	    new_param = param - lr * (update + wd * param)
35	    return new_param, m, v
36	
37	
38	launch_adamw_step_jit = jax.jit(
39	    launch_adamw_step, static_argnames=("lr", "beta1", "beta2", "eps", "wd")
40	)
41

1	"""Pallas/TPU launch glue for Prodigy.
2	
3	Algorithm: csrc/algorithms/prodigy.h
4	Self-contained — inlines the functional JAX implementation that previously
5	lived in supergrok2_jax_tpu/simple_optimizers_jax.py.
6	
7	On TPU the d_t update is fused into the JIT graph; no separate device-
8	resident scalar is needed.
9	"""
10	
11	from __future__ import annotations
12	
13	import jax
14	import jax.numpy as jnp
15	from typing import NamedTuple, Tuple
16	
17	
18	class ProdigyState(NamedTuple):
19	    """Per-parameter state for Prodigy."""
20	    exp_avg: jnp.ndarray
21	    exp_avg_sq: jnp.ndarray
22	    s_buf: jnp.ndarray       # distance-weighted accumulator
23	    param_init: jnp.ndarray  # initial parameter snapshot
24	    step: jnp.ndarray        # scalar int32
25	
26	
27	class ProdigyConfig(NamedTuple):
28	    """Prodigy hyperparameters."""
29	    lr: float = 1.0
30	    beta1: float = 0.9
31	    beta2: float = 0.999
32	    eps: float = 1e-8
33	    weight_decay: float = 0.0
34	    d_lr_init: float = 1.0
35	
36	
37	def init_prodigy_state(param: jnp.ndarray) -> ProdigyState:
38	    flat = param.reshape(-1)
39	    return ProdigyState(
40	        exp_avg=jnp.zeros_like(flat),
41	        exp_avg_sq=jnp.zeros_like(flat),
42	        s_buf=jnp.zeros_like(flat),
43	        param_init=flat.copy(),
44	        step=jnp.array(0, dtype=jnp.int32),
45	    )
46	
47	
48	def prodigy_step(
49	    param: jnp.ndarray,
50	    grad: jnp.ndarray,
51	    state: ProdigyState,
52	    config: ProdigyConfig,
53	    d_lr: float,
54	) -> Tuple[jnp.ndarray, ProdigyState, float]:
55	    """One Prodigy step. Returns (new_param, new_state, new_d_lr).
56	
57	    Distance-based adaptive LR estimation + Adam.
58	
59	    NOT ON THE LIVE FUSED-TU PATH — standalone EMA-`s_buf` reference only (no
60	    callers; the fused composition in _pallas_fused.py dispatches Prodigy through
61	    ``launch_prodigy_step`` below, which is the canonical fused-TU contract).
62	    Its d-estimate uses an EMA denominator (degree-1 in d), so the matching
63	    scale-free numerator here would be degree-1 (a single d power), NOT the
64	    degree-2 form of launch_prodigy_step. Kept as-is; see launch_prodigy_step.
65	    """
66	    step = state.step + 1
67	    p_flat = param.reshape(-1).astype(jnp.float32)
68	    g = grad.reshape(-1).astype(jnp.float32)
69	
70	    num = jnp.sum(g * (p_flat - state.param_init))
71	    den = jnp.sum(state.s_buf * jnp.abs(g))
72	
73	    # Keep d_lr as a device scalar — never force a host sync via float(...),
74	    # which would block the device queue and serialise the step.
75	    new_d_lr = jnp.where(den > 0, jnp.maximum(d_lr, num / den), d_lr)
76	
77	    new_s = config.beta2 * state.s_buf + (1.0 - config.beta2) * jnp.abs(g) * d_lr
78	    effective = g * d_lr
79	
80	    bc1 = 1.0 - config.beta1 ** step
81	    bc2 = 1.0 - config.beta2 ** step
82	
83	    new_ea = config.beta1 * state.exp_avg + (1.0 - config.beta1) * effective
84	    new_easq = config.beta2 * state.exp_avg_sq + (1.0 - config.beta2) * effective ** 2
85	
86	    step_size = config.lr / bc1
87	    denom = jnp.sqrt(new_easq / bc2) + config.eps
88	
89	    new_p = p_flat * (1.0 - config.lr * config.weight_decay) - step_size * new_ea / denom
90	
91	    new_state = ProdigyState(
92	        exp_avg=new_ea, exp_avg_sq=new_easq, s_buf=new_s,
93	        param_init=state.param_init, step=step)
94	    return new_p.reshape(param.shape), new_state, new_d_lr
95	
96	
97	def launch_prodigy_step(
98	    param: jnp.ndarray,
99	    exp_avg: jnp.ndarray,
100	    exp_avg_sq: jnp.ndarray,
101	    s_track: jnp.ndarray,
102	    param_init: jnp.ndarray,
103	    grad: jnp.ndarray,
104	    d_prev: float,
105	    beta1: float, beta2: float, eps: float, wd: float,
106	    bc1: float, bc2: float,
107	) -> Tuple[jnp.ndarray, jnp.ndarray, jnp.ndarray, jnp.ndarray, float]:
108	    """Per-tensor Prodigy step (fused-TU contract)."""
109	    delta = param_init - param
110	    r_sum = jnp.sum(grad * delta) * (d_prev * d_prev)
111	    # NOTE (audit): the numerator carries d² (degree-2) to MATCH the denominator's
112	    # d² so the estimate d_hat = r/s is scale-free (degree 0 in d). A degree-1
113	    # numerator (a single d_prev) made d_hat ∝ 1/d, which at the d0 = 1e-6 init
114	    # blew d up by ~1e6× in one step (catapult); the degree-2 form is VALIDATED
115	    # on H100 against the external prodigyopt 1.1.2 package (d tracks prodigyopt,
116	    # no catapult — see tests/hw/parity_gate_h100.py §2). The denominator is the
117	    # Prodigy-paper L1 norm Σ_j|d²·g_j| (== d²·Σ|g|), consistent with canonical
118	    # prodigy.h (per-element fabsf, i.e. L1) and the HIP backend.
119	    s_sum = jnp.sum(jnp.abs(grad)) * (d_prev * d_prev)
120	    candidate = r_sum / (jnp.abs(s_sum) + 1e-12)
121	    d = jnp.maximum(d_prev, candidate)
122	
123	    g_scaled = d * grad
124	    m = beta1 * exp_avg + (1.0 - beta1) * g_scaled
125	    v = beta2 * exp_avg_sq + (1.0 - beta2) * g_scaled * g_scaled
126	    update = (m / bc1) / (jnp.sqrt(v / bc2) + eps)
127	    new_param = param - d * (update + wd * param)
128	    new_s = s_track + d * grad
129	    return new_param, m, v, new_s, d
130

1	"""Pallas/TPU launch glue for Muon.
2	
3	Algorithm: csrc/algorithms/muon.h
4	Self-contained — inlines the functional Newton-Schulz implementation
5	that previously lived in supergrok2_jax_tpu/simple_optimizers_jax.py.
6	
7	2D weights: Newton-Schulz orthogonalization
8	1D parameters: AdamW fallback
9	"""
10	
11	from __future__ import annotations
12	
13	import functools
14	import jax
15	import jax.numpy as jnp
16	from jax import lax
17	from typing import NamedTuple, Tuple
18	
19	
20	class MuonState(NamedTuple):
21	    """Per-parameter state for Muon."""
22	    momentum_buf: jnp.ndarray
23	
24	
25	class MuonConfig(NamedTuple):
26	    """Muon hyperparameters."""
27	    lr: float = 0.01
28	    momentum: float = 0.9
29	    weight_decay: float = 0.0
30	    ns_steps: int = 5
31	
32	
33	def init_muon_state(param: jnp.ndarray) -> MuonState:
34	    return MuonState(momentum_buf=jnp.zeros_like(param))
35	
36	
37	def _newton_schulz_ortho(X: jnp.ndarray, ns_steps: int) -> jnp.ndarray:
38	    """Newton-Schulz orthogonalization (lax.fori_loop / scan-friendly form).
39	
40	    Muon paper coefficients: a=3.4445, b=-4.7750, c=2.0315.
41	    Iterates: X <- a*X + b*X(XᵀX) + c*X(XᵀX)²  (the quintic NS polynomial,
42	    identical to ``newton_schulz_iterate`` below). The previous third term
43	    ``c*X(XᵀX)`` was only cubic — a real divergence from the canonical Muon
44	    orthogonalization.
45	    Converges to the nearest orthogonal matrix.
46	
47	    NOTE: this is the scan-form twin of ``newton_schulz_iterate`` below (the
48	    unrolled form used by the fused-TU launcher). Both use the same Muon
49	    coefficients and produce mathematically equivalent results; the two forms
50	    coexist because lax.fori_loop (scan) is more XLA-efficient for the
51	    standalone reference path while the unrolled loop better matches the
52	    per-tensor fused-TU contract.
53	    """
54	    a, b, c = 3.4445, -4.7750, 2.0315
55	
56	    # fp32 accumulate on the MXU fast path at HIGHEST precision: keeps the
57	    # Newton-Schulz matmuls bit-stable vs the prior default-fp32 ``@``.
58	    _mm = functools.partial(
59	        jnp.matmul,
60	        precision=lax.Precision.HIGHEST,
61	        preferred_element_type=jnp.float32,
62	    )
63	
64	    def ns_body(_, X):
65	        AX = _mm(X.T, X)          # XᵀX
66	        AAX = _mm(AX, AX)         # (XᵀX)²
67	        return X * a + _mm(X, AX) * b + _mm(X, AAX) * c
68	
69	    return lax.fori_loop(0, ns_steps, ns_body, X)
70	
71	
72	def muon_step(
73	    param: jnp.ndarray,
74	    grad: jnp.ndarray,
75	    state: MuonState,
76	    config: MuonConfig,
77	) -> Tuple[jnp.ndarray, MuonState]:
78	    """One Muon step. Newton-Schulz orthogonalized momentum."""
79	    g = grad.astype(jnp.float32)
80	    new_m = config.momentum * state.momentum_buf + g
81	
82	    if param.ndim >= 2:
83	        X = new_m
84	        norm_val = jnp.linalg.norm(X)
85	        X_normed = X / jnp.maximum(norm_val, 1e-8)
86	        X_ortho = _newton_schulz_ortho(X_normed, config.ns_steps)
87	        update = X_ortho * norm_val
88	    else:
89	        update = new_m
90	
91	    new_p = param * (1.0 - config.lr * config.weight_decay) - config.lr * update
92	    return new_p, MuonState(momentum_buf=new_m)
93	
94	
95	def newton_schulz_iterate(
96	    X: jnp.ndarray, ns_steps: int, a: float, b: float, c: float
97	) -> jnp.ndarray:
98	    """Unrolled Newton-Schulz variant used by the fused-TU launcher.
99	
100	    This is the unrolled-form twin of ``_newton_schulz_ortho`` above (the
101	    scan-friendly form). Both use the same Muon coefficients (a=3.4445,
102	    b=-4.7750, c=2.0315) and produce mathematically equivalent results.
103	    """
104	    _mm = functools.partial(
105	        jnp.matmul,
106	        precision=lax.Precision.HIGHEST,
107	        preferred_element_type=jnp.float32,
108	    )
109	    for _ in range(ns_steps):
110	        AX = _mm(X.T, X)
111	        AAX = _mm(AX, AX)
112	        X = a * X + b * _mm(X, AX) + c * _mm(X, AAX)
113	    return X
114	
115	
116	def launch_muon_step(
117	    param: jnp.ndarray,
118	    buf: jnp.ndarray,
119	    grad: jnp.ndarray,
120	    lr: float,
121	    momentum: float,
122	    wd: float,
123	    ns_steps: int = 5,
124	    ns_a: float = 3.4445,
125	    ns_b: float = -4.7750,
126	    ns_c: float = 2.0315,
127	) -> Tuple[jnp.ndarray, jnp.ndarray]:
128	    """Per-tensor Muon step (fused-TU contract)."""
129	    # Canonical Muon momentum is plain SGD-momentum `buf = momentum*buf + grad`
130	    # (csrc/algorithms/muon.h, bindings.cpp muon_fused_step). The spurious
131	    # (1-momentum) factor shrank the gradient ~10x and diverged from the
132	    # source of truth.
133	    new_buf = momentum * buf + grad
134	    if param.ndim >= 2:
135	        frob = jnp.linalg.norm(new_buf) + 1e-8
136	        X = new_buf / frob
137	        X = newton_schulz_iterate(X, ns_steps, ns_a, ns_b, ns_c)
138	        max_dim = max(param.shape[-1], param.shape[-2])
139	        neg_lr_scale = -lr * 0.2 * jnp.sqrt(jnp.float32(max_dim))
140	        new_param = param * (1.0 - lr * wd) + neg_lr_scale * X
141	    else:
142	        new_param = param - lr * new_buf
143	    return new_param, new_buf
144

15	class GrokAdamWState(NamedTuple):
16	    """Per-parameter state for GrokAdamW."""
17	    exp_avg: jnp.ndarray       # first moment
18	    exp_avg_sq: jnp.ndarray    # second moment
19	    ema: jnp.ndarray           # gradient EMA for amplification
20	    step: jnp.ndarray          # scalar int32
21	
22	
23	class GrokAdamWConfig(NamedTuple):
24	    """GrokAdamW hyperparameters."""
25	    lr: float = 1e-3
26	    beta1: float = 0.9
27	    beta2: float = 0.999
28	    eps: float = 1e-8
29	    weight_decay: float = 1.0
30	    alpha: float = 0.98
31	    lamb: float = 5.0
32	    gradient_clipping: float = 10.0
33	
34	
35	def init_grokadamw_state(param: jnp.ndarray) -> GrokAdamWState:
36	    flat = param.reshape(-1)
37	    return GrokAdamWState(
38	        exp_avg=jnp.zeros_like(flat),
39	        exp_avg_sq=jnp.zeros_like(flat),
40	        ema=jnp.zeros_like(flat),
41	        step=jnp.array(0, dtype=jnp.int32),
42	    )
43	
44	
45	def grokadamw_step(
46	    param: jnp.ndarray,
47	    grad: jnp.ndarray,
48	    state: GrokAdamWState,
49	    config: GrokAdamWConfig,
50	) -> Tuple[jnp.ndarray, GrokAdamWState]:
51	    """One GrokAdamW step. EMA amplification followed by Adam."""
52	    step = state.step + 1
53	    g = grad.reshape(-1).astype(jnp.float32)
54	
55	    gnorm = jnp.linalg.norm(g)
56	    g = jnp.where(gnorm > config.gradient_clipping,
57	                  g * (config.gradient_clipping / (gnorm + 1e-12)), g)
58	
59	    new_ema = config.alpha * state.ema + (1.0 - config.alpha) * g
60	    effective = g + config.lamb * new_ema
61	
62	    new_ea = config.beta1 * state.exp_avg + (1.0 - config.beta1) * effective
63	    new_easq = config.beta2 * state.exp_avg_sq + (1.0 - config.beta2) * effective ** 2
64	
65	    bc1 = 1.0 - config.beta1 ** step
66	    bc2 = 1.0 - config.beta2 ** step
67	    step_size = config.lr / bc1
68	    denom = jnp.sqrt(new_easq / bc2) + config.eps
69	
70	    p_flat = param.reshape(-1)
71	    new_p = p_flat * (1.0 - config.lr * config.weight_decay) - step_size * new_ea / denom
72	
73	    new_state = GrokAdamWState(
74	        exp_avg=new_ea, exp_avg_sq=new_easq, ema=new_ema, step=step)
75	    return new_p.reshape(param.shape), new_state
76	
77	
78	def launch_grokadamw_step(
79	    param: jnp.ndarray,
80	    exp_avg: jnp.ndarray,
81	    exp_avg_sq: jnp.ndarray,
82	    ema: jnp.ndarray,
83	    grad: jnp.ndarray,
84	    alpha: float,
85	    lamb: float,
86	    lr: float,
87	    beta1: float,
88	    beta2: float,
89	    eps: float,
90	    wd: float,
91	    bc1: float,
92	    bc2: float,
93	) -> Tuple[jnp.ndarray, jnp.ndarray, jnp.ndarray, jnp.ndarray]:
94	    """Per-tensor GrokAdamW step (fused-TU contract)."""
95	    new_ema = alpha * ema + (1.0 - alpha) * grad
96	    g_amp = grad + lamb * new_ema
97	    m = beta1 * exp_avg + (1.0 - beta1) * g_amp
98	    v = beta2 * exp_avg_sq + (1.0 - beta2) * g_amp * g_amp
99	    update = (m / bc1) / (jnp.sqrt(v / bc2) + eps)
100	    new_param = param - lr * (update + wd * param)
101	    return new_param, m, v, new_ema
102	
103

def launch_supergrok2_step(
    param: jnp.ndarray,
    exp_avg: jnp.ndarray,
    exp_avg_sq: jnp.ndarray,
    mu_state: jnp.ndarray,
    slow_state: jnp.ndarray,
    grad: jnp.ndarray,
    expert_out: jnp.ndarray,
    sharpness: jnp.ndarray,
    A_log: jnp.ndarray,
    proj_W: jnp.ndarray, proj_b: jnp.ndarray,
    alpha: float, gru_decay: float, lamb_eff: float,
    lr: float, beta1: float, beta2: float, eps: float, wd: float,
    bc1: float, bc2: float,
) -> Tuple[jnp.ndarray, ...]:
    """Per-tensor SG2 step (fused-TU contract).

    Byte-faithful to csrc/algorithms/supergrok2.h::sg2_apply_step (the single
    source of truth, lines 395-438):

        mu_new     = gru_decay*mu_state + (1-gru_decay)*expert_out   (supergrok2.h:419)
        slow_new   = alpha*slow_state   + (1-alpha)*g                (supergrok2.h:423)
        smart_grad = g + alpha*mu_new + lamb_eff*slow_new            (supergrok2.h:426)
        m = beta1*exp_avg    + (1-beta1)*smart_grad                  (supergrok2.h:428)
        v = beta2*exp_avg_sq + (1-beta2)*smart_grad^2               (supergrok2.h:429)
        update = (m/bc1) / (sqrt(v/bc2) + eps)                       (supergrok2.h:436)
        p_new  = p - lr*(update + wd*p)                              (supergrok2.h:437)

    `expert_out` is the PEER expert output for the element (produced by the
    separate CSA/HCA+PEER meta-net launch; here it is an input, matching the
    kernel's `const float expert_out` argument). `alpha` is BOTH the mu/slow
    mixing coefficient AND the slow-EMA decay (supergrok2.h:388-394). The
    `lamb_eff*slow_new` grokfast term was previously DROPPED here (the step took
    no expert_out/slow_state/lamb_eff and used `smart = grad + alpha*mu_state`);
    restored to match the header — see supergrok2_sm90.cuh:555-573 and the
    parity reference ref_sg2_apply_step (tests/hw/test_reference_parity.py:237).
    """
    mu_new = gru_decay * mu_state + (1.0 - gru_decay) * expert_out
    slow_new = alpha * slow_state + (1.0 - alpha) * grad
    smart = grad + alpha * mu_new + lamb_eff * slow_new
    m = beta1 * exp_avg + (1.0 - beta1) * smart
    v = beta2 * exp_avg_sq + (1.0 - beta2) * smart * smart
    update = (m / bc1) / (jnp.sqrt(v / bc2) + eps)
    new_param = param - lr * (update + wd * param)
    return new_param, m, v, mu_new, slow_new

11 race optimizers' per-tensor ``launch_<opt>_step`` (the fused-TU contract math
in ``csrc/backends/pallas/launch_<opt>.py`` — the canonical TPU source per
``csrc/algorithms/SOURCE_OF_TRUTH.md``) is wrapped in a whole-array
``pl.pallas_call(..., interpret=True)`` and run on CPU against the fp64-accumulate
reference functions in ``tests/hw/test_reference_parity.py`` (transcribed 1:1 from
``csrc/algorithms/<opt>.h``).

Design (deliberately a MATH-parity harness, not a tiling harness):
  * ONE block over the whole array (BlockSpec defaults), so the test isolates the
    per-element optimizer math and is immune to tiling/pipelining bugs. Odd /
    non-multiple-of-8 shapes are still exercised via arbitrary array sizes; TPU
    tiling correctness is a silicon-day-1 item (see the day-1 checklist in the
    audit report / module docstring of csrc/fused/tpu_v6e).
  * fp32 kernel inputs vs the fp64 reference, at the SAME fp32-vs-fp64 tolerance
    discipline the GPU half of test_reference_parity.py uses (atol=1e-4,
    rtol=1e-3 — see test_kernel_matches_reference_gpu). 1e-9/1e-7 there is the
    fp64-vs-fp64 self-consistency band and would be wrong here.
  * Multiple sizes, seeds, NONZERO initial state, and several sequential steps for
    the stateful EMA optimizers (state threaded through both paths in lockstep).

    PYTHONPATH=. python3 -m pytest tests/tpu/test_pallas_parity_interpret.py -q

from csrc.backends.pallas.launch_adamw import launch_adamw_step

# fp32-vs-fp64 tolerance (matches the GPU half of test_reference_parity.py).
ATOL = 1e-4
RTOL = 1e-3

# Sizes: include odd, prime, and non-multiple-of-8 lengths.
SIZES = [7, 13, 16, 31, 64, 100]
SEEDS = [0, 1, 7]


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
#  Interpret-mode harness: wrap a pure-JAX launch fn in pl.pallas_call.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def _run_interp(fn, array_args, scalar_kwargs, n_out):
    """Execute ``fn`` inside a whole-array ``pl.pallas_call(interpret=True)``.

    ``array_args``  : tuple of jnp arrays passed positionally (first, in order).
    ``scalar_kwargs``: dict of python-scalar kwargs closed over by the kernel.
    ``n_out``       : number of array outputs ``fn`` returns.

    The kernel body reads every input ref whole, calls ``fn``, and writes each
    output ref whole. A single block (default BlockSpec) covers the whole array,
    so this validates math, not tiling.
    """
    out_shapes = tuple(
        jax.ShapeDtypeStruct(array_args[0].shape, jnp.float32)
        for _ in range(n_out)
    )

    def kernel(*refs):
        in_refs = refs[:len(array_args)]
        out_refs = refs[len(array_args):]
        vals = tuple(r[...] for r in in_refs)
        res = fn(*vals, **scalar_kwargs)
        if not isinstance(res, tuple):
            res = (res,)
        for o_ref, val in zip(out_refs, res):
            o_ref[...] = val.astype(jnp.float32)

    outs = pl.pallas_call(
        kernel,
        out_shape=out_shapes if n_out > 1 else out_shapes[0],
        interpret=True,
    )(*array_args)
    if n_out == 1:
        outs = (outs,)
    return tuple(np.asarray(o, dtype=np.float64) for o in outs)


def _t(np_arr):
    """numpy float64 -> torch float64 (reference input)."""
    return torch.from_numpy(np.ascontiguousarray(np_arr)).to(torch.float64)


def _close(got_np, ref_torch, *, atol=ATOL, rtol=RTOL, what=""):
    ref_np = ref_torch.detach().cpu().numpy().astype(np.float64)
    got_np = np.asarray(got_np, dtype=np.float64)
    ok = np.allclose(got_np, ref_np, atol=atol, rtol=rtol)
    if not ok:
        max_abs = float(np.max(np.abs(got_np - ref_np)))
        denom = np.abs(ref_np) + 1e-30
        max_rel = float(np.max(np.abs(got_np - ref_np) / denom))
        raise AssertionError(
            f"{what}: parity FAILED max_abs={max_abs:.3e} max_rel={max_rel:.3e} "
            f"(atol={atol}, rtol={rtol})")
    return float(np.max(np.abs(got_np - ref_np)))

@pytest.mark.parametrize("seed", SEEDS)
def test_prodigy_interpret_parity(size, seed):
    """Prodigy fused-TU contract: degree-2 partials -> d update -> Adam(d*g)."""
    r = _rng(seed)
    b1, b2, eps, wd = 0.9, 0.999, 1e-8, 0.0
    p = r.standard_normal(size).astype(np.float32)
    p_init = (p - r.standard_normal(size) * 0.5).astype(np.float32)  # drifted from init
    m = (r.standard_normal(size) * 0.1).astype(np.float32)
    v = np.abs(r.standard_normal(size) * 0.1).astype(np.float32)
    s_track = (r.standard_normal(size) * 0.1).astype(np.float32)
    d_prev = 0.3
    for t in range(1, 4):
        g = r.standard_normal(size).astype(np.float32)
        bc1, bc2 = 1.0 - b1 ** t, 1.0 - b2 ** t
        gp, gm, gv, gs, gd = _run_interp(
            _prodigy_wrapper,
            (jnp.asarray(p), jnp.asarray(m), jnp.asarray(v), jnp.asarray(s_track),
             jnp.asarray(p_init), jnp.asarray(g)),
            dict(d_prev=float(d_prev), beta1=b1, beta2=b2, eps=eps, wd=wd,
                 bc1=bc1, bc2=bc2),
            n_out=5)
        # Reference: compute d from the degree-2 partials, then the apply step.
        r_sum, s_sum = ref_prodigy_partials(_t(p), _t(p_init), _t(g), d_prev=d_prev)
        # launch_prodigy_step's d candidate guard uses |s_sum|+1e-12 (no early
        # return), so mirror that exactly here for an apples-to-apples d.
        d = float(max(d_prev, float(r_sum) / (abs(float(s_sum)) + 1e-12)))
        rp, rm, rv, rs = ref_prodigy_apply_step(
            _t(p), _t(g), _t(m), _t(v), _t(s_track),
            d=d, beta1=b1, beta2=b2, eps=eps, wd=wd, t=t)
        _close(np.array([gd[0]] if np.ndim(gd) else gd), torch.tensor([d]),
               what=f"prodigy d (t={t})")
        _close(gp, rp, what=f"prodigy p (t={t})")
        _close(gs, rs, what=f"prodigy s_track (t={t})")
        p, m, v, s_track = (gp.astype(np.float32), gm.astype(np.float32),
                            gv.astype(np.float32), gs.astype(np.float32))
        d_prev = d


def _prodigy_wrapper(param, exp_avg, exp_avg_sq, s_track, param_init, grad,
                     *, d_prev, beta1, beta2, eps, wd, bc1, bc2):
    """Adapt launch_prodigy_step (returns scalar d) to a whole-array kernel by
    broadcasting d to the param shape so it can be written to an output ref."""
    new_param, m, v, new_s, d = launch_prodigy_step(
        param, exp_avg, exp_avg_sq, s_track, param_init, grad, d_prev,
        beta1, beta2, eps, wd, bc1, bc2)
    d_arr = jnp.broadcast_to(jnp.asarray(d, jnp.float32), param.shape)
    return new_param, m, v, new_s, d_arr

    alpha = 0.5
    H = 32
    # phi_forward: x=[N,2] @ W1.T -> W1 is [H,2]; h @ W2[:,None] -> W2 is [H].
    W1 = (r.standard_normal((H, 2)) * 0.3).astype(np.float32)
    b1v = (r.standard_normal(H) * 0.1).astype(np.float32)
    W2 = (r.standard_normal(H) * 0.3).astype(np.float32)
    b2v = float(r.standard_normal())

    m = (r.standard_normal(size) * 0.1).astype(np.float32)
    v = np.abs(r.standard_normal(size) * 0.1).astype(np.float32)
    sharp = (r.standard_normal(size) * 0.5).astype(np.float32)
    momentum = (r.standard_normal(size) * 0.5).astype(np.float32)
    for t in range(1, 4):
        g = r.standard_normal(size).astype(np.float32)
        bc1, bc2 = 1.0 - b1 ** t, 1.0 - b2 ** t

            launch_supergrok11_step,
            (jnp.asarray(p), jnp.asarray(m), jnp.asarray(v), jnp.asarray(momentum),
             jnp.asarray(g), jnp.asarray(sharp), jnp.asarray(momentum),
             jnp.asarray(W1), jnp.asarray(b1v), jnp.asarray(W2)),
            dict(phi_b2=b2v, alpha=alpha, lr=lr, beta1=b1, beta2=b2, eps=eps,
                 wd=wd, bc1=bc1, bc2=bc2),
            n_out=4)

        _close(gp, rp, what=f"sg11 p (t={t})")

777	        inside from ``inputs``); ``params`` IS the model ``weights`` and

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
#  SuperGrok2 LIVE composition path (sg2_update) — the path that actually ships
#  via OPT_STEPS["supergrok2"], distinct from launch_supergrok2_step (the
#  per-element sg2_apply_step twin tested above, which is NOT yet in OPT_STEPS).
#
#  sg2_update runs the REAL CSA/HCA/PEER meta_net for smart_g, then the restored
#  grokfast tail (slow-EMA + lamb_eff) + layer_beta1 Adam, matching the
#  authoritative eager path supergrok2.py::_single_param_step:2388-2406. We do a
#  DIFFERENTIAL reconstruction (NOT a mock): run the same real meta_net_forward
#  in the reference so smart_g cancels bit-for-bit (fp32), leaving only the
#  grokfast+Adam tail to validate in fp64.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def _sg2_meta_weights(rng, dm=8):
    """NONZERO randomized meta-weights matching _pallas_fused.py's sg2 state
    builder shapes (lines ~949-979), so smart_g departs from g meaningfully."""
    def R(*shape, s=0.3):
        return jnp.asarray((rng.standard_normal(shape) * s).astype(np.float32))
    arrays = {
        "input_proj_W": R(dm, 2), "input_proj_b": R(dm),
        "csa_q_W": R(dm, dm), "csa_k_W": R(dm, dm),
        "csa_v_W": R(dm, dm), "csa_out_W": R(dm, dm),
        "csa_compress_w": R(8),
        "csa_idx_DQ": R(dm, 4), "csa_idx_UQ": R(4, dm), "csa_idx_K": R(dm, 4),
        "hca_q_W": R(dm, dm), "hca_k_W": R(dm, dm),
        "hca_v_W": R(dm, dm), "hca_out_W": R(dm, dm),
        "gru_W_z": R(4, 2 + 2 * dm + 4), "gru_W_r": R(4, 2 + 2 * dm + 4),
        "gru_W_h": R(4, 2 + 2 * dm + 4),
        "gru_b_z": R(4), "gru_b_r": R(4), "gru_b_h": R(4),
        "peer_query_Ws": R(2, dm, 4 + 2 * dm + 2),
        "product_keys_A": R(2, 4, dm // 2), "product_keys_B": R(2, 4, dm // 2),
        "expert_W1": R(16, 4, 1), "expert_b1": R(16, 4),
        "expert_W2": R(16, 1, 4), "expert_b2": R(16, 1),
    }
    structural = {
        "rescale": 1.0, "d_model": dm, "pk_dim": 4, "num_peer_heads": 2,
        "n_heads": 2, "csa_compress": 4, "csa_window": 8, "csa_topk": 4,
        "hca_compress": 4, "indexer_rank": 4, "gru_hidden": 4,
    }
    return arrays, structural


@pytest.mark.parametrize("size", [8, 16, 32])
@pytest.mark.parametrize("seed", SEEDS)
@pytest.mark.parametrize("gate_signal", [0.0, 0.6])
def test_supergrok2_live_update_parity(size, seed, gate_signal):
    """LIVE sg2_update tail parity (gate=0 catches the base-term half of the
    drift fix: effective_g must be smart_g, NOT the old gc + ...; gate!=0
    catches the restored grokfast slow-EMA term)."""
    from csrc.backends.pallas._pallas_fused import (
        sg2_update, meta_net_forward, _meta_weights_from_dict, MetaNetConfig)
    rng = _rng(seed)
    dm = 8
    arrays, structural = _sg2_meta_weights(rng, dm)
    meta_weights = dict(arrays)
    meta_weights.update(structural)
    layer_beta1, beta2, lr, wd, eps = 0.9, 0.999, 1e-3, 0.01, 1e-8
    lamb, ramp, alpha, grad_clip = 2.0, 1.0, 0.7, 1.0
    hyper = dict(layer_beta1=layer_beta1, beta2=beta2, lr=lr, wd=wd, eps=eps,
                 lamb=lamb, ramp=ramp, gate_signal=gate_signal, alpha=alpha,
                 grad_clip=grad_clip)

    p = (rng.standard_normal(size) * 0.5).astype(np.float32)
    st = {
        "exp_avg": (rng.standard_normal(size) * 0.1).astype(np.float32),
        "exp_avg_sq": np.abs(rng.standard_normal(size) * 0.1).astype(np.float32),
        "mu": (rng.standard_normal(size) * 0.1).astype(np.float32),
        "slow": (rng.standard_normal(size) * 0.1).astype(np.float32),
        "sharpness": (rng.standard_normal(size) * 0.3).astype(np.float32),
        "gru_state": (rng.standard_normal((size, 4)) * 0.1).astype(np.float32),
        "step": 2,
    }
    st = {k: (jnp.asarray(v) if isinstance(v, np.ndarray) else v)
          for k, v in st.items()}

    config = MetaNetConfig(
        d_model=dm, n_heads=2, csa_compress=4, csa_window=8, csa_topk=4,
        hca_compress=4, indexer_rank=4, num_peer_heads=2,
        num_experts=16, expert_hidden=4, gru_hidden=4, pk_dim=4, rescale=1.0)
    mnw = _meta_weights_from_dict(meta_weights)

    for _ in range(3):
        g = (rng.standard_normal(size) * 1.0).astype(np.float32)
        new_p, new_st = sg2_update(jnp.asarray(g), jnp.asarray(g), st,
                                   meta_weights, hyper)
        # Differential reference: same clip, same REAL meta_net (cancels in fp32),
        # then the grokfast+Adam tail in fp64.
        g32 = jnp.asarray(g)
        gnorm = jnp.linalg.norm(g32.reshape(-1))
        clip = jnp.minimum(1.0, grad_clip / (gnorm + 1e-12))
        gc = np.asarray(g32 * clip, np.float64)
        smart_g, _gru, _ = meta_net_forward(
            jnp.asarray(g) * clip, st["sharpness"], st["gru_state"], mnw, config)
        smart_g = np.asarray(smart_g, np.float64)
        slow0 = np.asarray(st["slow"], np.float64)
        ea0 = np.asarray(st["exp_avg"], np.float64)
        easq0 = np.asarray(st["exp_avg_sq"], np.float64)
        p0 = np.asarray(p, np.float64) if False else np.asarray(g, np.float64)  # params==g in this call
        p0 = np.asarray(g, np.float64)
        lamb_eff = lamb * ramp * gate_signal
        new_slow = alpha * slow0 + (1.0 - alpha) * gc
        eff = smart_g + lamb_eff * new_slow
        ea = layer_beta1 * ea0 + (1.0 - layer_beta1) * eff
        easq = beta2 * easq0 + (1.0 - beta2) * eff * eff
        step_i = int(st["step"])
        bc1 = 1.0 - layer_beta1 ** step_i
        bc2 = 1.0 - beta2 ** step_i
        update = (ea / bc1) / (np.sqrt(easq / bc2) + eps)
        exp_p = p0 - lr * (update + wd * p0)

        _close(np.asarray(new_p, np.float64), torch.from_numpy(exp_p),
               what=f"sg2_update live p (gate={gate_signal})")
        _close(np.asarray(new_st["slow"], np.float64), torch.from_numpy(new_slow),
               what=f"sg2_update live slow (gate={gate_signal})")

        # Non-vacuity: at gate!=0 the grokfast term must MOVE the result vs gate=0.
        if gate_signal != 0.0:
            hyper0 = dict(hyper); hyper0["gate_signal"] = 0.0
            p_nogf, _ = sg2_update(jnp.asarray(g), jnp.asarray(g), st,
                                   meta_weights, hyper0)
            assert not np.allclose(np.asarray(new_p), np.asarray(p_nogf),
                                   atol=1e-6, rtol=1e-6), (
                "grokfast slow term is vacuous (gate!=0 == gate=0)")
        st = new_st
